title: Pot knob with separate pointer skirt
prompt: Knob for a guitar-pedal pot with a separate skirt, so I can print the skirt in a contrasting colour and glue it on. Knob: 20 mm diameter, 16 mm tall, with a 1 mm x 45° chamfer round the top edge and a 6 mm hole, 12 mm deep, in the bottom for the knurled shaft (tight fit). Skirt: a 32 mm diameter, 2 mm thick disc with a 20.2 mm hole in the middle so it slides over the knob, and a small V notch in its rim as a pointer, 2 mm wide at the edge and 2 mm deep. Print them side by side: knob centred on the origin, skirt centred at X = 30, both standing on Z = 0.

hidden_tests.description: Evaluates cleanly and every body is a valid closed solid
Side by side: from X = −10 to 46, Y = ±16, 16 mm tall
The knob: 20 mm x 16 mm on the origin; volume ±0.3% checks the 6 mm x 12 shaft hole and the chamfer
The skirt: 32 mm x 2 mm at X = 30, with a V notch (4 flat faces: top, bottom and the two notch sides)
One 20.2 mm hole (20.1–20.4): the skirt slides over the 20 mm knob
The top edge is chamfered: one conical face

notes: Notch area = triangle (base 2, height √255 − 14) + rim segment beyond the chord at y = √255 (R²·acos(d/R) − d·1). Skirt bbox is 31.97 mm in Y because the notch removes the top of the rim.
